pages.text: The mathematics of things that change: rate equations, where they settle, and whether they stay there.

$(thing)Rates as Equations$(): the $(item)Integrator$() steps a rate equation forward. Set the step size and the method's order; the error must be under the recipe's tolerance, and too big a step blows up. It makes $(item)e Crystals$() (one of Euler's five constants) and the first machine $(thing)upgrades$().

Upgrades: use one on a multiblock's controller or a console machine to fit it (one per machine; fitting another hands the old one back). The $(item)Rate Table$() adds 20% products each cycle on top of precision: a perfectly tuned machine goes past perfect. The $(item)Stability Margin$() ($(thing)Stability$()) makes precision fall off half as fast.

$(thing)Enzyme Kinetics$(): the $(item)Enzyme Assay Bench$() measures an enzyme. Saturate it to 90% without choking it. $(item)Assayed Enzymes$() make Nutrient Broth and Stem Cell Cultures with far less; $(thing)Inhibition$() and $(thing)Cooperativity$() add a cheaper Stem Cell Culture and a steep S-curve (Porphyrin Oxygen Carriers, like haemoglobin).
$(thing)Euler's Formula$(): the Integrator turns π, e and rationals into the $(item)Imaginary Unit$(), i.
